main_text.p: vium non patiens ) ullus daretur : & tamen vadando alios ad pedtus ufque undis immersos, alios natando, utrofque toto corpore nudos, tædas verò sine flammis ferentes, ne conspici è longinquo possent, per noctis tenebras, qua hostium nemo expectaverat, istûc devenisse, & accensis repente tædis, summâ audaciâ non vulnera non mortem veritos, per medios hostes armatos & resistentes ad machinas velut lymphatas sese intulisse, easque incendio dedisse, quinetiam hostes tantâ audaciâ perculsos in fugam compulisse & eorum castra terrore complevisse, ac tandem re, ob quam venerant, patratâ, eadem via, qua venerant, & eodem modo ad suos revertisse: Scipionem ægrè fugam suorum sistere, & trepidationem comprimere potuisse : verumtamen sedatâ consternatione locum illum recuperasse, operibusque munivisse, impositisque ei quatuor armatorum millibus & machinis novis constructis, proxima urbis inde infesta habuisse[?]. Acta hæc vergente jam æstate. Per hyemem secutam scribit Appianus, Scipionem reliquos hostium in vicinâ regione feliciter debellasse, & infinitam eorum cædem edidisse, decem millia in servitutem abduxisse, oppida munita ce-pisse

page.notes: The scan is slightly blurred. The printed page number at top right is read as "91" but is uncertain. The long s is printed as f throughout and has been normalised to s. The word "habuisse" ends with a mark that may be a printed hook or a damaged letter, so it is marked [?]. The catchword "pisse" completes "ce-pisse" from the last line. The running head is read as printed.
